Reduced STAT1 signalling fails to deliver the full macrophage-activating program in response to IFN-gamma.
Partially activated macrophages fail to kill ingested mycobacteria, which replicate and disseminate.

nodes.description: Prolonged multidrug antimycobacterial chemotherapy is the mainstay for the infection itself, guided by species identification and susceptibility. Regimens combine agents such as rifampicin, isoniazid, ethambutol and a macrolide (clarithromycin), and refractory disease may require second-line agents such as levofloxacin. It treats the organism, not the immune defect, and courses are long because of the chronic, relapsing nature of the disease.

evidence.reference_title: Two cases of partial dominant interferon-γ receptor 1 deficiency that presented with different clinical courses of bacille Calmette-Guérin multiple osteomyelitis.
evidence.snippet: complete remission has since been achieved by combination antimycobacterial therapy, including levofloxacin.

nodes.description: The live BCG vaccine is the commonest trigger of disease, so it is contraindicated in an affected individual and should be withheld from at-risk relatives pending genetic testing. Early diagnosis allowing BCG to be avoided prevents BCG osteomyelitis.

evidence.reference_title: Early diagnosis of partial interferon-γ receptor 1 deficiency prevents the development of Bacille de Calmette et Guérin osteomyelitis.
evidence.snippet: He avoided BCG vaccination and has been disease-free since then.

nodes.description: Disease caused by the live M. bovis BCG vaccine strain after routine vaccination, ranging from local BCGitis to disseminated BCGosis, but in this disorder most characteristically manifesting as BCG osteomyelitis. It is the presenting event in vaccinated children.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic basis of patients with bacille Calmette-Guérin osteomyelitis in Japan: identification of dominant partial interferon-gamma receptor 1 deficiency as a predominant type.
evidence.snippet: partial dominant IFN-gammaR1 deficiency was the most common in Japanese patients who showed predisposition to curable BCG osteomyelitis.

nodes.description: Routine BCG immunisation is the sentinel exposure. The attenuated M. bovis BCG strain is harmless to immunocompetent infants but is not reliably contained by the partially deficient host, in whom it causes BCG disease — most characteristically osteomyelitis. In countries that vaccinate at birth the exposure precedes any possibility of diagnosis.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic basis of patients with bacille Calmette-Guérin osteomyelitis in Japan: identification of dominant partial interferon-gamma receptor 1 deficiency as a predominant type.
evidence.snippet: Heterozygous small deletions with frameshift (818del4 and 811del4) that are consistent with the diagnosis of partial dominant IFN-gamma receptor 1 (IFN-gammaR1) deficiency were detected in 3 unrelated patients.

nodes.description: Because the truncated receptor cannot be internalised and degraded, it is stably retained and overexpressed on the cell surface — measurably increased on monocytes. The accumulated non-functional chains compete with wild-type receptor for ligand, which is the structural basis of the dominant-negative effect and the diagnostic flow-cytometry signature.

evidence.snippet: Expression of IFN-gammaR1 on monocytes was significantly increased in all 3 patients.

nodes.description: Refractory atypical mycobacterial cutaneous granuloma is reported in 818del4 carriers, part of the soft-tissue extension of granulomatous inflammation.

nodes.description: A rarer non-mycobacterial manifestation. IFN-gamma-dependent macrophage activation is also required to control the dimorphic fungus Histoplasma capsulatum, and disseminated histoplasmosis with osteomyelitis is reported in the dominant partial form.

evidence.reference_title: Disseminated histoplasmosis in persons with interferon-gamma receptor 1 deficiency.
evidence.snippet: We identified a patient with recurrent disseminated Histoplasma capsulatum osteomyelitis who had an autosomal dominant form of IFN-gamma receptor 1 deficiency (i.e., a 4-bp deletion at or near base 818).

nodes.description: The truncated receptor cannot be phosphorylated to create a STAT1 docking site, so IFN-gamma binding produces reduced STAT1 phosphorylation and attenuated transcription of interferon-stimulated genes. Signalling is diminished but not abolished — partial STAT1 activation persists — which is the molecular correlate of the disease being partial rather than complete.

evidence.reference_title: The novel IFNGR1 mutation 774del4 produces a truncated form of interferon-gamma receptor 1 and has a dominant-negative effect on interferon-gamma signal transduction.
evidence.snippet: IFNgammaR1 was overexpressed on the surfaces of CD14-positive cells from the peripheral blood of this patient, and STAT1 phosphorylation in response to high doses of IFNgamma was partially deficient.

nodes.description: Regional or generalized lymphadenopathy with granulomatous, sometimes necrotizing, lymphadenitis accompanies mycobacterial disease and may be the presenting sign.

nodes.description: The initiating lesion is a single heterozygous frameshift deletion in exon 6 of IFNGR1 (the 818del4 hotspot, or the equivalent 811del4/774del4 alleles) that introduces a premature stop codon and removes the intracellular domain of the receptor. The wild-type allele is retained, so the cell expresses both full-length and truncated receptor chains.

evidence.reference_title: The novel IFNGR1 mutation 774del4 produces a truncated form of interferon-gamma receptor 1 and has a dominant-negative effect on interferon-gamma signal transduction.
evidence.snippet: Dominant forms of IFNgammaR1 deficiency are known to be associated with mutations that introduce a premature stop codon in the intracellular domain of IFNgammaR1.

nodes.description: The organism-level consequence is recurrent or disseminated infection by intracellular pathogens a competent IFN-gamma response would contain: the BCG vaccine strain, environmental non-tuberculous mycobacteria (chiefly Mycobacterium avium complex), Mycobacterium tuberculosis, and — rarely — the dimorphic fungus Histoplasma capsulatum. This node initiates the infectious phenotypes; bone and lymph node, macrophage-rich sites with slow local clearance, are characteristically involved.

evidence.snippet: In dominant patients, 30 (79%) had environmental mycobacterial disease and 11 (73%) of 15 BCG-vaccinated patients had BCG disease.

nodes.description: IFN-gamma is the signal that licenses macrophages to kill the intracellular mycobacteria they harbour. With signalling blunted below the protective threshold, infected macrophages are only partially activated and cannot restrict mycobacterial growth. This is the shared final mechanism of MSMD, reached here through an impaired response to the cytokine rather than through impaired production of it.

evidence.reference_title: Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial diseases: State of the puzzle.
evidence.snippet: almost all genetic etiologies of MSMD alter the interferon-gamma (IFN-γ)- mediated immunity by impairing or abolishing IFN-γ production or the response to this cytokine.

nodes.description: The prototypical manifestation. BCG or environmental mycobacterial infection presents as unifocal or, characteristically, multifocal osteomyelitis of long bones, vertebrae, ribs and skull, often without other organ involvement. Mycobacterium avium complex osteomyelitis is the classic form, and bone-only disease occurs almost exclusively in the dominant partial rather than the recessive complete form.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical features of dominant and recessive interferon gamma receptor 1 deficiencies.
evidence.snippet: M avium complex osteomyelitis was more frequent in dominant than in recessive patients (22/28 [79%] vs 1/8 [13%], p=0.002), and this disorder without other organ involvement arose only in dominant patients (9/28 [32%]).

nodes.description: Mycobacterium avium complex is the commonest environmental mycobacterial agent, causing disseminated infection with multifocal osteomyelitis and necrotizing granulomatous lymphadenitis.

nodes.description: Because residual receptor function is present, adjunctive subcutaneous recombinant IFN-gamma engages the retained wild-type receptor and augments the macrophage-activating signal; it is added to antibiotics in refractory disease. This is the therapeutic dividing line within MSMD, and it is where the dominant partial form differs from the recessive complete form, in which the response to IFN-gamma is abolished and hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation is the treatment option.
